clue.text: New team doctor, a philosophical type

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the following word is rearranged into a fresh order

blocks.note: the word team, letters rearranged
a physician is a medical doctor

explanation.surface: A sports club hires a new medic who turns out to be a thoughtful sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphysician studies metaphysics, the branch of philosophy dealing with being and reality, so is a philosophical type.

clue.text: Like some alloying — city police hypersensitive, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the phrase is matched by how it is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police, and allergic means hypersensitive

explanation.surface: A grumble that a city's police force reacts badly, like a metal blend.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Met allergic' quickly and it sounds like METALLURGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgy is the science of metals, including combining them, so alloying is a metallurgic process.

clue.text: Amount of heat head of Harrow used during school session

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
something used during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: first letter of Harrow
a school term is a teaching session

explanation.surface: A headmaster's warmth spent across a school term.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, which helps the school surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, formerly used in British gas billing, equal to 100,000 British thermal units.

clue.text: Quietly passed on and given unexpected promotion

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a matter referred is passed on to someone else

explanation.surface: An employee quietly moved along and then surprisingly bumped up.
explanation.walkthrough: To prefer someone is an old sense of to promote them; the 'unexpected' adds colour to the surface rather than meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefer in the older sense means to advance someone to a higher office or rank.

clue.text: Dairy product giving husband energy over in nomad's tent

indicators.note: turned over means turned back to front, so these letters run the other way
being in something means placed within it, so one group sits inside the other

blocks.note: h is the standard abbreviation for husband
go means energy or vigour
a yurt is the round tent of Central Asian nomads

explanation.surface: A dairy product handed over to a husband in a nomad's tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' applies to both husband and energy together, and the reversed pair lodges after the tent's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is fermented milk, a staple product of the dairy.

clue.text: Bar disheartened architect finally left

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter of the word
finally points to the very end letter of the word

blocks.note: Inigo Jones was a celebrated English architect
last letter of left

explanation.surface: A dejected architect walked out of the bar at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones (1573-1652) designed the Banqueting House in London; removing his name's middle I leaves INGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: Lack of knowledge of good woman visiting fashionable church

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so these letters are put within the other pair

blocks.note: in means fashionable
g is an abbreviation for good
Nora is a woman's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worthy woman calls at a trendy church, knowing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' only links; 'good woman' visits the pair made of the fashionable word and the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is the state of not knowing, a lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Disappointing score, one inspired by new libretto initially

indicators.note: breath that is inspired is drawn in, so one letter goes inside the others
initially points to the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: n is short for new
I is the Roman numeral one
first letter of libretto

explanation.surface: A new opera libretto gets a poor mark from critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, a score of zero that disappoints any team.

clue.text: Eyesore some tomfool Yankee erected first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An American fool built something ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' looks like an ugly building, but it is literal: a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Charmingly interacting with lady dropping leaflet, for example

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: engaging with others means interacting with them
taken as written
an advertising leaflet is an example of an ad

explanation.surface: A lady handing out flyers chats pleasantly with passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AD from LADY to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Engagingly means in an attractive, winning way, which is to say charmingly.

clue.text: Burning torch an essayist coated in iron and gold

indicators.note: a thing coated in something is wrapped by it, so it sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A writer is plated in metal like a blazing torch.
explanation.walkthrough: Only iron coats the essayist; the gold follows after, so the chemical symbols do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, typically made of several thick wicks dipped in wax.

clue.text: Buzz brought about by short time in farm

indicators.note: being in something means placed within it, so the short unit goes inside the verb

blocks.note: hr is the short form of hour
to till land is to farm it

explanation.surface: The excitement of a brief stint working on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is a feeling of excitement, the same as a thrill.

clue.text: Coffee served outside below key washing-place

indicators.note: a thing outside other letters wraps around them, so the drink surrounds the rest

blocks.note: a latte is a milky coffee
under means below
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A café serving coffee beneath a key spot where people do their washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette is a self-service place with coin-operated washing machines for clothes.

clue.text: Lower level press employee returning pastries with hesitation

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for pastries is read backwards

blocks.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper
tarts are pastries
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker brings back pastries, hesitating at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A substratum is an underlying layer, a stratum lying below another.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment worn by only child, perhaps

blocks.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes that are worn are on

explanation.surface: A vest worn by a child with no siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn by' looks like a container instruction, but 'by' just places ON next to the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single individual, and an only child is one example of being on one's own.

clue.text: Obsession of woman entertaining native of Muscat, possibly

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest takes them in, so the woman's name holds the other word

blocks.note: Mona is a woman's name
Muscat is the capital of Oman

explanation.surface: A woman fixated on hosting a visitor from the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is an excessive preoccupation with one thing, that is, an obsession.

clue.text: Intelligence organisation originally in North America

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word
being in something means placed within it, so the letter sits inside the place

blocks.note: n is short for north
first letter of organisation
the US is America

explanation.surface: A spy agency that began on the American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence organisation' reads as one phrase like the CIA; 'Intelligence' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for common sense or practical intelligence, from Greek for mind.

clue.text: Opposed to article leading to mother's ruin

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin

explanation.surface: Taking a stand against an item that drove a mother to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is dialect for against, so to be agin something is to be opposed to it.

clue.text: Vague implication reportedly losing force

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the phrase is matched by its sound

blocks.note: dim means vague, and an innuendo is a sly implication

explanation.surface: A hazy suggestion that seems to fade as it is passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim innuendo' said aloud runs together into DIMINUENDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminuendo in music is a gradual decrease in loudness, so the sound is losing force.

clue.text: Failing to notice girl during golf

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
in means during, as in 'in the night'
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Overlooking a young woman out on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing something means overlooking it, not seeing it at all.

clue.text: Boarding vessel, choose the best oars

indicators.note: boarding a ship means going on board, so the verb's letters sit inside the vessel

blocks.note: SS is steamship
to cull is to select from a group

explanation.surface: Getting on a boat and picking the finest oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculls are a pair of oars worked by one rower.

clue.text: Middle Easterner's second car

blocks.note: s is short for second
Audi is a German car maker

explanation.surface: An Arab who owns another vehicle as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saudi is a native of Saudi Arabia, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Dull headgear ultimately — old, it may be felt

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: sombre means dull or dark
last letter of headgear
o is short for old

explanation.surface: A dreary hat whose age is something you can sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as a verb, but it is the cloth: the definition says the hat may be made of felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed hat commonly made of felt or straw.

clue.text: Relax about current exam

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the other letter

blocks.note: to rest is to relax
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Advice to calm down about the upcoming test.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after a failure, a British term.

clue.text: Member of order such a train transported

indicators.note: things transported are moved about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A monk carried along by a train of this sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carthusian is a monk of the Carthusian religious order, founded by St Bruno.

clue.text: A period of time in Scottish port

blocks.note: taken as written
yr is the short form of year

explanation.surface: Spending a while in a harbour town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only links the wordplay to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a town and harbour on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Animal shelter situated at end of forest

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: set means placed or situated
last letter of forest

explanation.surface: A burrow placed on the edge of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow of a badger, its underground home.

clue.text: Ongoing struggle, administering East Sussex town!

blocks.note: running a business means administering it
Battle is the East Sussex town at the site of the Battle of Hastings

explanation.surface: A long fight to manage a small town on England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle, in East Sussex, grew up around the abbey built where the 1066 Battle of Hastings was fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A running battle is a continuing conflict that goes on over a long time.
